harmonicFunction: Fm9 (i9) - Velvety, dark tonic minor with the added 9th (G) providing sophisticated jazz color
Bbm7 (iv7) - Minor subdominant initiating the smooth circle-of-fifths harmonic descent
Eb9 (bVII9) - Dominant ninth functioning as the secondary dominant pulling toward Ab major
Abmaj7 (bIIImaj7) - Relative major tonic offering radiant, fleeting warmth
Dbmaj7 (bVImaj7) - Lyrical submediant chord continuing the stepwise bass motion
Gm7b5 (iiø7) - Half-diminished chord establishing classic jazz-noir tension
C7#9 (V7#9) - Altered dominant containing the raised leading tone (E) and sharp 9th (D#) that pulls forcefully into Fm9

techniques.name: Lush Jazz Chord Voicings & Drop-2 Navigation
techniques.description: Fingerpicking four-note drop-2 jazz chord voicings across strings 4, 3, 2, and 1, emphasizing color tones (9ths, major 7ths, and altered #9s) with delicate bare-finger articulation

notes: Fret Fm9 with index barre at fret 1, ring finger on fret 3 string 5, and pinky on fret 3 string 1 (the added 9th G)
Form Eb9 with root on fret 6 of string 5: 6-5-6-6-X
Grip C7#9 (the 'Hendrix chord') at fret 3: X-3-2-3-4-X, letting the tension of the #9 (D#) resolve smoothly
Pluck with thumb and fingers simultaneously to sound all voices in unison without a strummed drag
Keep strings muted cleanly when not speaking to maintain pristine studio clarity
sequence: Pluck the low root with the thumb on beat 1
Sound upper color tones with fingers 1, 2, and 3 on the upbeat
Release fret-hand tension for a gentle, rounded acoustic decay
Shift smoothly along the fretboard through the circle-of-fifths sequence
tips: Keep your fret-hand fingers arched high on their tips to avoid muting adjacent open voices
Use a hollowbody or Stratocaster neck pickup with tone rolled back slightly to 7 for round, smoky warmth
Practice the chord changes in pairs (Fm9 to Bbm7, then Eb9 to Abmaj7) at 60 BPM

techniques.name: Counterpoint Fills & Volume-Swell Shading
techniques.description: Mark Knopfler's masterclass in musical restraint: weaving understated, vocal-style single-note fills and delicate volume swells into the spaces between the saxophone melody

notes: Listen intently to the saxophone phrasing; never play while the horn is carrying the primary melody
Answer the saxophone lines with 2-to-4 note melodic fills in F minor pentatonic
Use horizontal wrist vibrato on sustained notes to simulate the warmth of a horn vibrato
Employ subtle pinky volume swells to soften the attack of chord entries
sequence: Wait for the saxophone phrase to resolve on beat 4
Enter on beat 1 with a gentle single-note slide into the 8th fret C note on string 1
Release smoothly back down through the F minor scale
Fade into silence as the next vocal line begins
tips: In jazz ballads, what you don't play is as important as what you do play
Pair with a lush stereo chorus and studio plate reverb for a pristine 1980s studio sheen

commonMistakes: Playing with high gain or overdrive; this song demands pristine, velvety clean jazz headroom
Overplaying lead fills while the iconic saxophone is carrying the melody, creating cluttered sonic competition
Muting adjacent strings with lazy fret-hand finger angles instead of arching cleanly on fingertips
Rushing the relaxed, nocturnal 76 BPM ballad pulse
